summary.en: Israel continues to expand its presence in southern Lebanon, building roads and opening bases while striking Qantara and conducting overflights that wounded a Lebanese footballer and detaining a 65‑year-old retired engineer. Hezbollah has arrested five members in Batroun, kept artillery fire on Israeli positions and begun cash payments to war victims and displaced families. Lebanon has asked Syria to extradite suspects in the killing of former Iraqi MP Ahmed al-Alwani, while UNRWA funding cuts deepen hardship for Palestinian refugees in Lebanon. 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel fortsetter å utvide sin tilstedeværelse i sørlige Libanon, bygger veier og åpner baser mens de angriper Qantara og gjennomfører overflyvninger som såret en libanesisk fotballspiller og arresterte en 65‑år gammel pensjonert ingeniør. Hezbollah har arrestert fem medlemmer i Batroun, holdt artilleribrann på israelske posisjoner og begynt å betale kontantstøtte til krigsofre og fordrevne familier. Libanon har bedt Syria om å utlevere mistenkte i drapet på den tidligere irakiske MP Ahmed al-Alwani, mens kutt i UNRWA-finansieringen forverrer vanskelighetene for palestinske flyktninger i Libanon. 4 335 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
